sections.subtitle: Five segments, FY2024 vs FY2025 -- Precision Machinery is the semiconductor (CMP/vacuum pump) segment and the most cyclical and highest-margin of the five

charts.title: Segment Revenue
charts.annotation: Only disclosed for FY2024-FY2025 under the current segment structure; earlier years used a different segmentation and are not comparable.

charts.title: Segment Operating Profit
charts.annotation: Precision Machinery alone generated more operating profit than any other two segments combined in both years -- and management's FY2028 target for it is a 20%+ operating margin.

charts.title: Segment Operating Margin
charts.annotation: Precision Machinery's margin is structurally the highest of the five and the most exposed to the semiconductor WFE capex cycle; the other four are comparatively defensive, replacement- and O&M-driven businesses.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Ebara Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Ebara Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Ebara Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Ebara Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Ebara Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Ebara Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Ebara Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Ebara Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
Ebara reports five segments: Building Service & Industrial (pumps for buildings/water), Energy (compressors/turbines incl. Elliott Company), Environmental Solutions (waste incineration plants), Infrastructure (large pumps for public works) and Precision Machinery (semiconductor CMP tools and vacuum pumps).

For Ebara Corporation: Precision Machinery is the semiconductor-equipment business -- it is tied to wafer-fab-equipment (WFE) capex, not to the industrial/infrastructure cycle the other four segments share. FY2025 Precision Machinery revenue grew far faster than the group (AI-driven WFE demand) while Energy was roughly flat.

What to watch:

  • Precision Machinery's share of group revenue rising or falling with the WFE cycle
  • Energy segment swings tied to oil & gas/power capex and large one-off project timing
  • Only FY2024-FY2025 are shown -- older filings used a different segment structure, not a gap in the data

segmentProfit.title: Segment operating profit
segmentProfit.content:
Operating profit by the same five segments. Mix matters as much as growth here: Precision Machinery is both the fastest-growing and the highest-margin segment, so a shift in revenue mix toward it flows through to group operating profit faster than revenue growth alone would suggest.

For Ebara Corporation: management's FY2028 targets for Precision Machinery alone are 20%+ operating margin and 25%+ ROIC -- materially above the group average -- so this chart is the direct check on whether that segment is carrying the group's margin expansion.

What to watch:

  • Precision Machinery profit growing faster than its revenue (operating leverage in the up-cycle)
  • Energy segment profit swings from shipment/service delays or project losses (flagged as a risk in H1 FY2026)

segmentMargin.title: Segment operating margin
segmentMargin.content:
Operating profit divided by revenue for each segment -- the clearest view of which parts of Ebara's portfolio are structurally higher-margin versus cyclical-but-thin.

For Ebara Corporation: Precision Machinery's margin sits well above the other four and is the segment most exposed to the semiconductor WFE cycle -- the qualitative analysis and DCF both flag a WFE slowdown as the key downside risk precisely because it would hit the group's highest-margin segment hardest. Building Service & Industrial, Infrastructure and Environmental Solutions are comparatively defensive, replacement- and public-works-driven businesses with thinner but steadier margins.

What to watch:

  • Precision Machinery margin compressing as a leading indicator of WFE digestion/oversupply
  • Whether margin gains are broad-based or concentrated in the one cyclical segment

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Ebara Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Ebara Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
